purpose: workflow pilot verification only, not an accuracy or detection-limit claim

declared_checks.replicate_identity: two spectra of one recipe must share composition, profile, energy axis, the full expected spectrum and the six component spectra, and differ only in Poisson counting noise
declared_checks.six_component_identity: sum(components) = sum(expected_counts) and sum(components) + sum(outside_window) = detected_signal_before_window_counts, tolerance 1e-6 relative
declared_checks.window_loss_budget: declared before the run: outside/detected <= 0.01 per spectrum
declared_checks.profile_matches_candidate_file: every sealed profile must equal P3_candidate.json field for field
declared_checks.energy_window_matches_candidate: every sealed energy_window must equal the window the delivered dataset.energy_window() derives from P3_candidate.json
declared_checks.composition_sums_to_100: used_percent must sum to 100 within the documented strict tolerance of 1e-6 percentage points
declared_checks.support_table: the delivered core.element_support() is called with original_percent keys minus {Als, Alt} union the modelled weights (core.py:406), so the table documents the elements of this recipe, not a fixed 32-target panel. Accepted rule, checked per spectrum: the key set must reproduce that call exactly, every target with positive used mass must have an entry, and O is counted separately as a non-target key.
declared_checks.matrix_line: every spectrum with Fe mass must model Fe KL3_LINE

loss_side_attribution.conclusion: the discarded band is the high-energy side, from 16.680 keV to the 20 keV tube voltage (unscattered continuum plus its Rayleigh and Compton tail; a photon above 17.2 keV Compton-scattered at 90 degrees still lands above the window). Nothing can sit below the 0.296 keV lower edge because the delivered source grid starts at 1 keV

line_system_check.meaning: per scenario/interference-pair group: how many of the 200 spectra model each watched line, how many of those place it inside the recorded window, and the largest expected net detected counts that line reaches in that group. Modeled counts are bounded by how many spectra actually contain the element, listed in elements_present. Line existence is not resolvability, and a modeled line with a small net count is not detectability either.
line_system_check.expected_detected_counts: primary_emitted + secondary_emitted, multiplied by the same factors core.simulate() applies (incident_photons_s * live_time_s * current_uA / reference_current_uA * solid_angle / 4pi, then detector_efficiency * exit-air transmission), so the number is an expected net count over the whole live time
